content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I'm looking to set up a notification or alarm on my [product_name] operator device to alert me if ethernet communication between the operator device and the [product_name] controller is interrupted. I tried using the diagnostic ethernet error bit V984.0, but this doesn't work in my setup. My operator device and [product_name] controller are linked through an ethernet switch, so if the connection between the operator device and the switch fails (while the controller-switch link is fine), I don't receive any notification. Is there any way to trigger an alarm or notification when the operator device-to-controller link is lost? I am using [product_name] version [article_no] and [product_name] HMI Basic Panel.

You could try creating a tag on the operator device that sends a signal to the network input when pressed. Then invert this signal and set up a text alarm, so when the connection breaks, you should receive the alarm on the controller. I'm not certain this will work, but every idea is worth trying.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking a more robust solution than the built-in ethernet error detection to reliably alert when communication between their operator device and controller is lost, particularly when only a specific segment of the network fails.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a dependable notification or alarm on the operator device whenever the communication link with the controller is disrupted, regardless of which part of the network connection fails.
